site.description: Christen Jacquottet is a creative technologist in Dallas building AI, realtime voice and web AR experiences for brands, nonprofits and attractions.

profile.name: Christen Jacquottet
profile.headline: From imagination to implementation.
profile.summary: I turn wild ideas into real things. Part design, part engineering, constantly asking ‘what if?’
profile.focus: I build AI products, voice experiences, and interactive software—from the first question to the details that make it work.
about: I grew up in France, studied Computer Science and Digital Media at Taylor University, and joined LERMA/ in Dallas as a contract software engineer in 2022. I became Digital Project Manager on the He Gets Us websites in 2023, moved into creative technology, and have held the Creative Technologist title since May 2025. Today I build the AI, voice and AR work the agency pitches and ships.

That has meant a classification backend for a Super Bowl campaign, a talking William Booth for The Salvation Army, an AR attraction at Reunion Tower and an AI World Cup host. I also lead internal AI education for LERMA/'s senior creatives, guest-lectured on AI and creativity at SMU, and serve on the AAF Dallas board.
Outside work I photograph, follow markets, and build small tools for myself.

projects.title: Invite LERMA
projects.summary: A live World Cup companion: a digital version of LERMA/'s Chief Growth Officer who called matches in English or Spanish, handled interruptions, and drew 84 match bookings in a month, our own testing included. The core worked in under a week; Muse by Clios and LBB covered it.

projects.title: What Are You Sick Of?
projects.summary: The 2025 He Gets Us Super Bowl campaign asked America what it was sick of. I built the AI backend that classified 113,000+ answers into themes, replied to each person, and fed the national map.

projects.title: Gateway to Dallas
projects.summary: Award-winning web AR for Reunion Tower's GeO-Deck. I was the only developer on a team of about ten: pick a place on a map, step through a portal into a captured garden, find a hidden sunflower.

projects.title: William Booth AI
projects.summary: I led the technical build of a talking William Booth for The Salvation Army: a voice prototype in 2024, a phone version unveiled at Mirren Live 2025, used for brand, strategy and training work.

projects.title: HOA Bud
projects.summary: A freelance AI product for HOA property managers: upload the governing PDFs, ask questions in plain language, and get answers that cite the page. Plus a Flutter app for residents.
projects.client: Don't Mess With Texas Property Management

projects.title: AI Bartender Experience
projects.summary: An iPad bartender that writes a cocktail recipe with GPT and photographs it with DALL·E. I built it for LERMA/'s Christmas party, then rebranded it for the pitch that won Hornitos.

projects.title: RAGformation
projects.summary: Box Award at LlamaIndex's Agentic RAG-a-thon: 458 participants, 100+ submissions, under 48 hours. Our team built a cloud architecture advisor, and I architected the retrieval service behind it.

projects.title: Drafty
projects.summary: A time-automation system for LERMA/ employees that rebuilds a workday from calendar, timers, Git, Teams and email, then separates substantiated allocations from those needing confirmation. Live submission remains disabled.

projects.title: ThoughtSpot Embedded Analytics SDK Demo
projects.summary: A multi-client analytics portal built in three weeks: ThoughtSpot Liveboards, Search and the Spotter AI analyst inside one branded Next.js shell, with row-level security keeping every client to its own data.

projects.title: Jesse, the He Gets Us Assistant
projects.summary: A conversational assistant for He Gets Us's skeptical, spiritually curious audience, built so a sensitive message never reaches the model. I built the guarded RAG pipeline in Dify, and the creative team uses it to write.

projects.title: LERMA/HQ Virtual Office
projects.summary: I had never used Roblox. In three days I wrote the Blender script that moved a 10,000+ part architect's model into it, then built a full game around LERMA/'s new Dallas office, played at a company happy hour.

projects.title: DMWTPM Website
projects.summary: The website for a Dallas–Fort Worth HOA management company, with Notion as the CMS so the client's own team edits pages, services and service areas without a developer. Live at dmwtpm.com.
projects.client: Don't Mess With Texas Property Management

projects.title: Digimodel VRM Avatars
projects.summary: I designed and built custom VRM avatars for LERMA/ clients including Avocados From Mexico, Jim Beam and Interstate Batteries, each ready for Zoom, streaming, AR and web metaverses.

projects.title: LERMA/ ARound Experience
projects.summary: A 2024 web AR experience that reveals Dallas landmarks around LERMA/'s West End office. I built the bridge between Immersal's VPS and 8th Wall myself, the first step toward Gateway to Dallas.

projects.title: Retrospect
projects.summary: Create an AI version of your younger self or a historical figure, then interview it live in a video room. One session joins LiveKit, OpenAI, ElevenLabs and Hedra.

projects.title: Bring on the Stronger Connection
projects.summary: In 24 hours, my team and I turned Xfinity's Wi-Fi reliability into a dating story with Hinge. The entry placed 2nd nationally in Digital at the 2024 U.S. Hispanic Young Lions.

projects.title: Ad-Verse Weekly
projects.summary: A two-day prototype for an advertising newsletter: a Gemini Computer Use agent handles browser logins, and a TipTap editor supports human review. AI summaries and email delivery remained unfinished.

projects.title: AI Focus Group Rooms
projects.summary: A research lab where a moderator invites several AI personas into a live video room. Built in a week as my first LiveKit room with AI participants, and the precursor to Invite LERMA.

projects.title: THE SKUPER
projects.summary: A four-day experiment in how browsers really authenticate a request: why a server-side fetch got a 403 and the same call from a logged-in tab didn't, turned into a working paste-and-export tool and a Chrome extension.

projects.title: Salvation Army Minecraft Food Pantry
projects.summary: In 2023 I built and hosted a playable Salvation Army food pantry in Minecraft, where NPCs explained the mission, filled typed food requests and pointed players to a real donation page.

projects.title: Avocado Ripeness Detector
projects.summary: A March 2023 experiment in pointing a phone at an avocado to judge ripeness, through color heuristics, a trained TensorFlow classifier, and a React interface for browser inference. The model integration remained unfinished.

projects.title: Running OpenAI's Symphony on Real Tickets
projects.summary: I pointed OpenAI's open-source Symphony at my team's Linear tickets. Over six weeks, eight routine issues across eight repos became branches and pull requests I reviewed and merged.

projects.title: Content Relevance Analyzer
projects.summary: Visitors searched He Gets Us and found nothing. I built the embedding pipeline that matched those dead-end searches to the articles that answered them, and mapped what the library was missing.

projects.title: RAG Crawler
projects.summary: A May 2024 Python tool that turns any website into clean Markdown for an AI to read, then measures it to pick the right chunk size for retrieval.

projects.title: Mining Bridge
projects.summary: A 2022 research project to automate a Bitcoin mining payout: carry each NiceHash payment across to Ethereum through RenVM and split it by weight in a Solidity vault.

projects.title: No-Loss Charity
projects.summary: A 2021 DeFi design for giving without losing your money: donors deposit stablecoins, keep a 1:1 claim on them, and vote each week on which charity gets the interest.

projects.title: SideXSide
projects.summary: A college team prototype that matched actors with readers for self-taped auditions. We specced a two-sided service with a $4 plan and reading credits, then built it in Flask.

projects.title: Dream Links
projects.summary: A 2020 senior-project app concept that matched someone's dream with a neighbor who could help, like a kid building a go-kart and a retired engineer in the same town.

projects.title: UniRides
projects.summary: A 2018 student venture to fix getting around a small college town: match Taylor students who need a ride with classmates already driving that way, with a fare built from the cost of gas.

projects.title: StudentAdviseStudent
projects.summary: A 2019 pitch to change how students pick a major: match high schoolers with current college students who already made that choice, free for students and paid for by universities.
